## Pass 13 (2026-09-19). Instrument A runs at stack scope, and THE PAIR TRACK FAILS ONLY IN COMPOSITION.

`of3t-gradients` `adbfdaca3`, three instruments and two bisects under `perf/of3t_gradients/`.

**Scope discipline first, because it decides how the result may be quoted.** Every artifact
carries `reference_is_the_frozen_bundle: false` and says so in words: *"self-generated float64
reference, upstream's own PairFormerBlock. of3t-reference's BUNDLE-MIN is the only reference a
PUBLISHED equivalence claim may use; this run validates the harness so that when the bundle
lands the only new thing is the data."* That is exactly the instruction it was given and exactly
the right way to label a pre-bundle run. **Nothing here is the campaign's equivalence claim.**

### R36. Every pair-track sub-module passes alone; the assembled block fails by an order of magnitude.

`bisect_grad.py`, block 2, 64 tokens, bar 0.05, identical probe through the identical matcher:

| sub-module, alone | worst relative |
|---|---|
| `tri_mul_out` | **0.0172** |
| `tri_mul_in` | **0.0156** |
| `pair_transition` | **0.0092** |
| `tri_att_start` | 0.1389 |
| `tri_att_end` | 0.1449 |

**In the assembled block every pair-track tensor reads 4.3e-01 to 1.4e+00**, while the single
track passes in the same run at 6.1e-03 to 6.4e-02.

So three of five pair-track sub-modules are comfortably inside the bar in isolation and the
composition is an order of magnitude outside it. **Passing sub-modules do not compose into a
passing block**, and a campaign that had only ever measured modules — which until this pass is
all this one had done — would have reported a clean result. That is the sharpest argument yet
for why §3's claim has to be made at model scope and not assembled from parts.

### R37. The triangle-attention gradient miss is attributable to the fp32-softmax path, and NOT to the pair-bias scaling.

From the same bisect, two arms the commit message did not foreground:

- `tri_att_start` **0.1389 -> 0.0428** with fp32-softmax off; `tri_att_end` **0.1449 -> 0.0524**.
  A ~3x improvement that brings both to the edge of the 0.05 bar. The fp32-softmax path is
  where the triangle-attention gradient error lives.
- `tri_att_end_scaledbias` **0.1450** against `tri_att_end` 0.1449. **Scaling the bias changes
  nothing.**

That second arm is an independent confirmation of my pass-6 analysis (R27/K34) from the
gradient side. I argued that `scale_pair_bias=False` is *correct* for `TriangleAttention` — the
defect is in `AttentionPairBias` on the single track — and that flipping the shared flag would
break the pair track. A row that did not know that argument measured the pair track with the
bias scaled and found it makes no difference: **the lever is not there**, which is what "False
is correct here" predicts. Two routes, same conclusion.

It also pins a cost onto R11's fp32-softmax path, which until now was known only as "had no
backward at all". It has one, and it is the largest single contributor to the triangle-attention
gradient error.

### K41. An instrument found two defects in ITSELF before it found any in the model, and both were silent.

- **`PairformerLayer` accumulates with `ttnn.add_`**, so reusing the discovery forward's input
  for the taped forward starts the taped run from block 0's *output*. It presents as a
  **5.6e-01 forward divergence**, i.e. as a model defect, not as a wiring bug.
- **K28 priced again, harder.** On a 0.05-scale unit-normal draw their block 0 reads
  `d|z|/|z| = 1.000` — the residual contributes nothing, so **every module downstream runs 148x
  outside its regime**. Warming the probe through their own float64 blocks first brings the
  forward to s 2.3e-03 and z 2.8e-02. A shape-correct input is not a valid input, and this is
  the third time this campaign has paid for that.

### §3a's second half is closed. K22's 1660 out-of-scope are placed.

`bijection_device.py`: what the built model **holds** is a further transform of the flat dict the
remap produces — a transpose, a second fusion built in `__init__`, a cache materialised on the
first call. `TriangleMultiplication` fuses four in-projections and `linear_g` into one 640-wide
`_gp_gout_cache`; `TriangleAttention` fuses q, k, v, the gate and the pair-bias projection into a
544-wide `qkvgb_weight` whose last band is **tile padding**. Matched by exact bf16 value with
every candidate confirmed elementwise, **so a fingerprint collision yields an unmatched tensor
rather than a wrong mapping** — the right failure direction for a matcher.

**53 of their 57 per-block tensors placed.** The 4 absent are `AttentionPairBias` q/k/v and the q
bias, which live in a fused qkv **the composed path carries no gradient for** — consistent with
`instrument_t_traj`'s excluded set and not a new gap.

## Pass 14 (2026-09-19)

### CORRECTION TO R37, AND IT IS MINE. The scaled-bias arm confirmed nothing.

In pass 13 I read `tri_att_end_scaledbias` 0.1450 against `tri_att_end` 0.1449 as *"an
independent confirmation of my pass-6 analysis from the gradient side"* — the argument being
that the lever is absent because `scale_pair_bias=False` is already correct for
`TriangleAttention`.

`of3t-gradients` looked at the same arm more carefully and it is right: flipping the flag at
that site moves **the forward** only 2.390e-02 -> 2.388e-02. **If the flag reached the bias the
forward would move by roughly sqrt(24)**, and it does not move at all. So the flag **does not
reach the internal pair-bias projection at that site**, the arm tested nothing, and it says
nothing about R27 in either direction.

A null result has two readings — *the setting is already right*, or *the experiment never
touched the thing* — and I took the flattering one because it agreed with an argument I had
made two passes earlier. The forward reading was in the same artifact I was quoting from and
discriminates between them. **R27 and K34 stand on the pass-6 source analysis alone**, which is
unaffected; what is withdrawn is the claim of a second, independent route to it.

### R38. fp32_softmax costs 3.2x on the triangle-attention weight gradient, under a 12 % forward change.

Same module, same warmed probe, same float64 reference, the flag alone:

| | fp32_softmax on | off |
|---|---|---|
| `tri_att_start` worst gradient | **1.389e-01** | **4.283e-02** |
| `tri_att_end` worst gradient | **1.449e-01** | **5.239e-02** |
| `tri_att_start` forward | 2.610e-02 | 2.923e-02 |
| `tri_att_end` forward | 2.390e-02 | 2.677e-02 |

**A 3.2x change in the gradient under a 12 % change in the forward.** That is the shape of error
a forward comparison structurally cannot see, and it is the clearest vindication the campaign
has produced of §3d-bis — the forward and the gradient are different instruments with different
sensitivities, and passing one says little about the other.

`openfold3_trunk.py:139` ships `fp32_softmax=True` and **OF3 is the one model on that route**, so
this is OF3-specific and corroborates R11 from the gradient side.

### R39. Triangle attention INJECTS the error; it does not inherit it.

The z-only cotangent isolates the pair track and moves the median from **8.630e-01 to
2.850e-01**, leaving an ordering that is **not monotone in backward depth**. If the error were
inherited from upstream modules and merely amplified, the ordering would track depth. It does
not, so the error enters at triangle attention.

### R40. The in-place pair residual is REFUTED as the cause, and recorded rather than dropped.

Aliasing `ttnn.add_` to `ttnn.add` for the whole process leaves **every figure bit-identical**,
so the in-place accumulation is not what makes the assembled block fail. A refuted hypothesis
kept on the record is worth as much as a confirmed one here — K41 had made `ttnn.add_` a
plausible suspect, and without this arm the next row would have spent a pass on it.

### K42. A null result has two readings, and the flattering one is not the default.

The generalisable form of this pass's correction, and it is the orchestrator's own mistake so it
is worth stating plainly.

When a lever is flipped and nothing moves, that is either **"the setting was already correct"**
or **"the lever was never connected to the thing"**. Those are opposite conclusions and the
measurement alone does not distinguish them. I took the first because it agreed with an
argument I had made two passes earlier, and it was the second.

**The discriminator is almost always cheap and usually already in the artifact.** Here it was
the forward reading sitting in the same JSON: flipping the flag moved the forward 2.390e-02 ->
2.388e-02, where a flag that actually reached a pair bias would have moved it by roughly
sqrt(24). One number, already measured, settles it.

So: **before reading a null as confirmation, name the observable that would move if the lever
WERE connected, and check it moved.** A lever with no measured effect on anything is an
untested lever, not a validated setting. This is the same family as §3e — a check that cannot
fail proves nothing — applied to a control rather than to a gate.

## Pass 15 (2026-09-19). D1's fix exists, shaped correctly, and is still UNMEASURED end to end.

### R41. `scale_pair_bias` is split, and the split is default-preserving by construction.

`of3t-pairbias` `bb59a9730`. `PairformerLayer` and `Pairformer` gain
`tri_att_scale_pair_bias: bool | None = None`, and
`tenstorrent.py:8877` resolves it as

    tri_scale = scale_pair_bias if tri_att_scale_pair_bias is None else tri_att_scale_pair_bias

**Verified rather than taken on report:** the default is `None`, the fallback is the old value,
and `grep` across `tt_bio/` finds exactly two callers naming the new parameter —
`openfold3_trunk.py:144` and `openfold3_confidence.py:98`, both
`scale_pair_bias=True, tri_att_scale_pair_bias=False`. So Protenix-v2, Boltz-2, BoltzGen and AF2
are **bit-identical by construction**, not by measurement, which is the stronger guarantee and
the right shape for a shared constructor.

That arrangement is exactly the opposite-values one R27/K34 said was needed: the token-level
`AttentionPairBias` gets the bias **pre-baked** (`True`) because its kernel folds the bias inside
its own score scale, and `TriangleAttention` keeps it **unscaled** (`False`) because it adds the
bias outside. One flag could never express both.

Block 0 against a float64 reference of the formula, real `of3-p2-155k` weights, golden inputs:
**AttentionPairBias 5.7577e-02 -> 1.7795e-02 relative L2, PCC 0.998522 -> 0.999977.**

### What is still owed, and it is the whole point of that row.

**No end-to-end number exists.** D1 is a defect in *shipped inference* — the token pair bias at
0.204 of reference in all 48 trunk blocks — and the fix now changes what every OpenFold3 fold
returns. What decides whether that is urgent, and what Moritz needs in order to decide anything,
is **the change to a real fold in Angstrom with the seed floor beside it**. A block-0 relative
L2 and a PCC are not statements about the structures users get.

The row's gate enforces this: its `FOLD:` field is rejected without a seed floor. It stays
release-gated and on its branch until that number exists, and this ledger does not describe D1
as fixed — it describes the fix as **written and unmeasured**.

Also still owed from the same brief: **one measurement each for the other four models**.
"Bit-identical by construction" is a strong argument and it is not a measurement; the campaign
has already been burned once by "Protenix trains, so Protenix must be fine" (R30), and the
cheap confirmation is the byte-identical inference control `of3t-tape` established — same
forward, same sha256, from a detached `origin/main` checkout on the same card.

## Pass 17 (2026-09-19). THE BUNDLE'S GRADIENT IS HELD: 99.86 % of its tensors are exactly zero, and it looked valid.

### R42. `of3t-reference` retracted its own gradient file, and every surface signal said it was fine.

`020c6cbab`. The float64 step-1 gradient has **`grad is not None` for all 4,147 parameters**, a
plausible **global norm of 4.642245878270448**, and a **finite-difference check passing at
1.08e-04** — and **only six tensors in it are non-zero**. The whole 48-block pairformer trunk,
the MSA module, the input and template embedders and **737 of the diffusion module's 738
tensors are exactly zero**. The six survivors are in every case **the last Linear of a branch**,
which is what a gradient looks like when the activations feeding that layer are **detached**.

**Their own path is fine, and the control proves it:** driven through `OpenFold3AllAtom` and
`pl.Trainer` in fp32, **4,850 of 4,890 state-dict tensors moved over 20 steps**. So the defect is
in the direct-call path `bundle_min.py` uses — most likely in the float64 mode that neutralises
their fp32 autocast and their unconditional `.float()`, i.e. **the code that had to exist for
float64 to run at all**.

Batch, seed, `w0`, draws and the presence map **stand**. The gradient file does not, and the
manifest now says so rather than letting a consumer find out by getting a clean-looking answer.
I have withdrawn my own instruction to `of3t-gradients` to consume it.

**This is the third distinct arrival of the same failure**, and it is the one PROTOCOL §3b was
written against: `zero-filled-missing-gradient-hides-an-untrained-model`. First as R21 (weights
not leaves, backward returns, nothing raises), then as R30 (AF2 at 0 of 184), now as a reference
whose gradient is 99.86 % zero while presenting a plausible norm. **The failure mode is not
"gradients are wrong", it is "gradients are absent and everything downstream still computes."**

### K44. A finite-difference spot-check of N entries cannot detect that most TENSORS are zero.

The methodological cause, and it is general. The FD validation sampled **16 entries**. On this
batch **99.9 % of individual gradient entries are exactly zero** — a 56-token sample padded to
the crop leaves most channels masked — so sampling entries uniformly finds agreement almost
everywhere by construction, and **16 draws cannot distinguish "correct and mostly zero by
masking" from "broken and mostly zero by detachment"**.

**And the sampling rule makes it sharper than "too few samples".** `MANIFEST.json` records it:
*"entries with |analytic| >= 1e-6, because 99.9 % of individual entries are exactly zero on a
padded 56-token batch"*. So the check **conditioned its sample on the analytic gradient already
being non-zero** — a filter that is entirely reasonable for avoiding a 0/0 relative error, and
which makes the instrument **structurally incapable of detecting a gradient that is wrongly
zero**. It only ever looked inside the six surviving tensors.

**The general rule: a validation that samples where the quantity is non-zero cannot find the
places it is wrongly zero.** Stratify by tensor, take at least one entry per tensor, and report
coverage as **the fraction of TENSORS touched** rather than a count of entries. "16 entries, max
relative 1.08e-04" reads like strong validation and is compatible with 4,141 tensors being
identically zero. Where a tensor has no entry above the floor, that absence is **the finding**
and must be reported, not skipped as unsamplable.

I quoted that 1.08e-04 into the evidence scoreboard as validation of the bundle. That line is
now corrected.

### K45. The determinism floor is measured, and a file hash is the wrong comparator for two bundles.

Two processes, same seed, same batch, same box: **loss and global gradient norm bit-identical,
4,141 of 4,147 gradient tensors bit-identical, worst per-tensor relative L2 1.8768e-16** — and
**the file sha256 still differs**.

So the manifest hash does what it is for — confirming a consumer **fetched the bytes intact** —
and must never be read as a comparator between two independently generated bundles, where a
mismatch would flag a disagreement **fourteen orders of magnitude below the 5.0e-02 bar**.
Integrity in transit and equivalence of content are different questions and one hash answers
only the first.


### R43. Two manifests differing only in case, and the stale one says the bundle is fine.

`perf/of3t_reference/bundle_min/` holds **both** `MANIFEST.json` (6.4 KB, authoritative, carrying
`status: GRADIENT ARTIFACT ON HOLD -- only 6 of 4147 parameter tensors carry a non-zero
gradient`) **and** `manifest.json` (11.3 KB, older, reporting `n_with_gradient: 4147,
n_absent: 0` with **no hold marker at all**).

On a case-sensitive filesystem both exist and a consumer reading the lowercase name gets the
reassuring, stale one. The bundle README and my own brief both refer to "the manifest" without
fixing the case. **A hold notice that only one of two same-named files carries is not a hold
notice**, and this is the same family as every other finding this pass: the surface signal says
valid.

Flagged to `of3t-reference` to delete or redirect the stale file. Until it does, the audit
asserts the hold status directly so the composition cannot quietly carry a bundle whose
authoritative manifest says do not use it.

## Pass 18 (2026-09-19). Three corrections, two of them mine.

### R44. My canonical bundle path was stale, and the brief kept asserting it as "verified".

The pass-6 amendment named `/home/ttuser/of3t/bundle_min/`. The pass-9 amendment **overrode it**
with `/home/moritz/of3t_bundle/bundle_min/` and called that path "verified" — which it was, at
the moment I ran the check. `of3t-reference` then consolidated onto the pass-6 path, and my
brief went on asserting a location that had ceased to exist until `of3t-gradients` arrived and
found nothing there.

Re-verified this pass: `/home/moritz/of3t_bundle/` **does not exist on qb2**;
`/home/ttuser/of3t/bundle_min/` holds the bundle. Canonical path corrected in the brief.

**The lesson is about how a verified fact is written down, not about the check.** "Verified" in
a brief reads as permanent and is a claim about one moment. A path, a host, a lease, a free-disk
figure — all of them rot, and a brief that asserts one without telling the reader to re-check it
will be believed long after it stops being true. The correction tells the row to re-check on
arrival rather than trust the line.

### The bundle itself is in better order than it looked, and the row's discipline is why we know.

`MANIFEST.json` carries a **per-file `on_qb2` flag**: batch, draws and presence map present with
matching sha256; **`grads_f64.pt` and `w0.pt` marked `on_qb2: false, sha256: "pending-transfer"`**
— produced and verified on the A100, the copy interrupted and re-running. And R43 is **fixed**:
`manifest.json` was renamed `run_record.json` so it can no longer be mistaken for the
publication on a case-sensitive filesystem.

`of3t-gradients` **hashed before reading anything** and reported two absent artifacts instead of
comparing against what was there. That is the amendment doing its job.

### R42's first hypothesis is REFUTED by the row that proposed it.

`of3t-reference` re-ran `bundle_min.py` at `--dtype float32`, with the autocast and `.float()`
neutralisation inactive: **still 6 of 4,147 non-zero gradient tensors**. So the float64
workarounds are **not** the cause and the direct-call path is — constructing `OpenFold3` and
`OpenFold3Loss` and calling `loss.backward()` — while their own runner moves 4,850 of 4,890
tensors over 20 steps on the same model and batches. Next bisect candidates are what the runner
does and a bare call does not: `setup('fit')` with `_identify_confidence_params`, the EMA
construction, and Lightning's batch transfer in place of the script's `move()`.

### R45. The gate had a hole shaped exactly like honest reporting, and the row that found it reported it.

`_of3t_donecheck.py`'s placeholder regex caught "not yet measured", "TBD" and "pending" but not
**"remaining", "left to <row>", "for the next pass"** — which are precisely the phrasings
`worker.sh` *recommends* for honest non-completion, and therefore precisely the ones that turn

**said so instead of doing it**, and its own verdict is PARTIAL.

Widened, scoped to the per-row `measured` fields so the general convention is untouched.
Verified by effect: the gate now rejects that row's document and still passes this one.

**Consequence handled:** that row had already concluded under the weaker gate while its central
deliverable is blocked on a transfer in flight, which would have left instrument A ownerless

## Pass 19 (2026-09-19). The orchestrator's own summary fields had drifted, and I caught it the way I catch everyone else's.

### R46. My honest-scope fields described the campaign as it stood seven passes ago.

`PROVES`, `DOESNOT`, `GAP` and `VERDICT` are the four fields a reader actually reads, and the
gate checks only that they **exist**. Mine still said the frozen bundle "does not exist yet"
(published pass 12), that the shared weight-discovery seam is "unfixed in the library"
(`of3t-leaves` closed it and concluded), that the §3a manifest "covers 3,275 of 4,935 with 1,660
needing a per-module remap entry point" (the device half closed it and 763 of those 1,660 turned
out to be bitwise duplicates), and that the campaign had "nine rows, two concluded" (ten and
six).

**The irony is the point.** I built `audit_evidence.py` to re-read 31 scoreboard figures from
their artifacts on every compose, precisely because *"a transcription drifts silently, because
both it and its source look like prose"* — and never applied that discipline to my own summary,
which is the one document written entirely by transcription from the ledger.

All four rewritten against the ledger. The current position, stated so it cannot be over-read:
**the state-free half of the update rule is verified exactly and the model-dependent half is
verified only on single modules** — and at stack scope the pair track is not merely unverified
but **actively refuted**, since sub-modules inside the bar compose into a block an order of
magnitude outside it.

### R47. And I immediately committed R43 in my own state doc.

Splicing the new fields in left the **old `GAP` and `VERDICT` still present at the foot of the
file** — two of each, the stale pair contradicting the current pair, in a document whose whole
job is to say where the campaign stands. That is exactly the defect I had recorded one pass
earlier as R43, where `MANIFEST.json` said ON HOLD and `manifest.json` said fine.

Removed, with a line in the file saying why rather than silently. **A superseded record left in
place is worse than no record**, because a reader who finds the stale one has no way to know it
is stale — and the two failure modes are identical whether the duplicate is a JSON file
differing in case or a heading repeated 600 lines down.

The generalisable form, and it is now twice-earned: **when you replace a summary, delete the
thing you replaced in the same edit.** An append-only habit is right for a ledger, where entries
are dated and ordered, and wrong for a status field, where only the current value is true.

## Pass 20 (2026-09-19). The merge-gate question, answered: `wk/of3t` is near-disjoint from TRAIN, and TRAIN's conflicts are with main.

I flagged a cross-campaign hazard in pass 3 — that `wk/train-i-run` was 87 commits ahead and
might collide with this campaign on `tt_bio/train/optim.py` — and never closed it. Closed now,
and the answer is better than expected in one direction and worse in another.

**No TRAIN branch touches `optim.py` at all.** `wk/train-i-run`, `wk/train-orchestrator` and
`wk/train-ad-tripwire3` all read **0** for that file. The pass-3 worry was unfounded.

**File overlap is one file.** `wk/of3t` touches 205 files, the TRAIN branches 126 between them,
and the intersection is exactly **`docs/training.md`**.

### R48. But a trial merge conflicts on THREE files, and two of them are nothing to do with OF3T.

Trial-merging into a detached `wk/of3t`:

- `wk/train-i-run` -> conflicts on **`README.md`, `docs/training.md`, `tt_bio/train/cli.py`**
- `wk/train-orchestrator` -> conflicts on **`docs/training.md`**

`wk/of3t` touches `README.md` **0 times** and `tt_bio/train/cli.py` **0 times**. The cause is the
merge base: `origin/wk/of3t` bases at `bd643929a`, which is main's head, while
`origin/wk/train-i-run` bases at **`350773d09`** — an older main. Between those two points
**main itself** committed 4 times to `README.md`, 1 to `cli.py` and 3 to `docs/training.md`.

So those two conflicts are **`train-i-run` against main's own progress**, surfacing in this trial
only because the trial merges into a branch that already contains main's head. **Merging OF3T
does not make TRAIN harder to merge; TRAIN is already stale against main**, and the only genuine
OF3T-versus-TRAIN overlap is one documentation file.

That is decision-relevant for the merge gate: the branches can be taken in either order, and
whoever takes `train-i-run` will be reconciling it with main regardless of what this campaign
does.

### K49. A file-overlap analysis by three-dot diff is only valid when the branches share a merge base.

The method I used first — `git diff --name-only origin/main...X` per branch, then intersect —
predicted **one** conflict and the trial merge produced **three**. Three-dot diff is computed
against each branch's **own** merge base, so for a branch based on an older main it silently
omits everything main changed since, and the conflicts that follow get misattributed to whichever
branch you happened to be merging into.

**Check the merge bases before intersecting file lists, and prefer a trial merge to an overlap
computation when the answer matters.** A trial merge in a throwaway worktree costs seconds and
cannot be wrong about what git will do.

## Pass 21 (2026-09-19). THE END-TO-END NUMBER EXISTS, and it splits two ways that must not be averaged.

### R49. D1's fold delta, measured with the full discipline, and the answer is not a single number.

`of3t-pairbias`. 1UBQ, 76 aa, **production CLI with a searched MSA**, 5 diffusion samples,
**nine seeds per arm**, shipped arm from a **detached `origin/wk/of3t` checkout on the same
Blackhole p300c** (card 2, **AICLK 1350 MHz sampled during the fold**):

| | shipped | split |
|---|---|---|
| rank 0 vs the experimental structure | **0.782 A** | **1.245 A** |
| best of five vs the same | **0.679 A** | **0.629 A** |
| lever, arm vs arm at matched seed | **1.204 A mean**, range 0.439-1.626 | |
| **seed floor, this target's own, 36 pairs** | **0.324 A mean**, range 0.011-0.734 | |

**The lever is 3.7x the seed floor, so it is outside noise** — which is exactly why the gate
demanded the floor beside the delta.

**And it splits two ways that must not be averaged: the corrected trunk SAMPLES BETTER and
SERVES WORSE.** Best-of-five improves 0.679 -> 0.629 while rank 0 degrades 0.782 -> 1.245,
because on **6 of 9 seeds the confidence head picks a 1.59 A sample with a 0.56 A sample sitting
in the same batch of five**. pLDDT rises over the same runs, 0.7162 -> 0.8014.

So fixing the trunk makes the model better and the product worse. **Shipping the trunk fix alone
would degrade what users get**, and the honest reading is not "the fix is bad" but "there is a
second defect downstream of it that the first was masking."

### R50. D1's TriangleAttention half is REFUTED, and it was my claim.

`AttentionPairBias`: False **5.7577e-02** / PCC 0.998522, True **1.7795e-02** / PCC 0.999977
against a float64 transcription of OF3's own formula. **True is right, a 3.2x error reduction,
and D1's token-side claim holds.**

`TriangleAttention`: False **3.4222e-02**, True **3.4287e-02**. **The flag is inert.** The
mechanism is named rather than inferred: both routes divide out what the load-time bake
multiplied in — `bias_scale_inv = 1.0/self._bias_scale` at `tenstorrent.py:7658`, and
`ttnn.multiply(bias, self.scale/self._bias_scale)` at 7647 and 7683 — so `_bias_scale` cancels
and only its bf16 rounding survives. Confirmed end to end: **reverting the confidence head's
tri override moves the served structure by 0.000 A on five seeds**.

**So K34's "the two classes need OPPOSITE values" is half wrong and the half is mine.** The
token side needed `True`; the triangle side does not care, and the `tenstorrent.py` comment
citing *"0.892 folded against 1.000000 unscaled"* describes a lever the forward now cancels.
`of3t-gradients` had already measured a 2e-05 forward move there and I recorded it as saying
"nothing either way" — it was in fact the first sighting of this, and a second row had to
measure it end to end before I accepted it.

**The split itself remains right engineering**: it is what let the token side take `True`
without touching the triangle side. Only my justification for its second half was wrong.

### The MODELS control is how a "no change" claim should be made.

Boltz-2, BoltzGen, Protenix-v2 and AF2, each from its own checkpoint with its own production
flags, one fixed forward, same card, this branch against detached `origin/wk/of3t`: **all four
byte-identical**. And the control that makes that mean anything — **`--tri 0` changes all three
Pairformer digests, while `--tri 1` did not, because those models already default True**. A
control that cannot break the check proves nothing, and this row built one that could.

### K50. Their diffusion rollout is priced: 0.0496 s per step plus 0.083 s hoisted fixed cost.

`of3t-perf`, rungs 4/12/20 reading **0.286 / 0.669 / 1.080 s** once a discarded warm-up call
absorbs the process's first sampler compile. Monotonic, least squares over all three rungs, max
residual **9 ms**. The fit puts their 20-step mini rollout at **1.075 s against 1.080 s measured
directly**, which is the agreement a ladder exists to produce. Same run reproduced the trunk
stages in a second process — prefix 7.20 s against 7.18 s, a cycle 2.43 s against 2.42 s — so
**the 384-token trunk cycle holds to about 0.3 % across processes**. Card 3 qb2 p300c, AICLK
median **1350 sampled during**, loadavg 4.4-10.2.

Still no s/step against their GPU, because that baseline does not exist yet — but our side now
has a decomposed, cross-process-stable cost model rather than a single number.

### K51. Three splice bugs in three passes, and the third doubled a 66 KB document.

My own editing method has now failed three times in a way worth recording, because the campaign
keeps finding the same class in other people's code.

- Pass 19: replacing four summary fields left the **old `GAP` and `VERDICT` still in the file**
  (R47).
- Pass 20: an insert anchored on `BRANCH: **\`wk/of3t\` is pushed at \`366daa360\`` raised
  `AssertionError` because the line had changed — caught, but only by the assert.
- Pass 21: `i = t.index("PASS 20.") if "PASS 20." in t else None` then
  `t[:i] + NEW + t[i:]`. There was no `PASS 20.` heading, so `i` was **`None`**, and Python's
  slicing turned that into `t[:None] + NEW + t[None:]` — **the whole 66 KB document
  concatenated to itself**. The DONE_CHECK passed the doubled file, because every field it
  looks for was present twice.

**`None` is a valid slice index and means "the whole thing", so a guard that yields `None` on
failure silently converts a missing anchor into a duplication.** The assert-based version failed
loudly and was the better bug. Repaired by detecting the doubled header and truncating, then
moving the new block into chronological position.

The transferable rule, and it is the same one the gate lessons keep producing: **make the
failure mode of an edit loud.** An anchor that is absent must raise, never default — and a
size check after a supposedly small edit (66 KB -> 128 KB) would have caught this before the
gate did not.

## Pass 22 (2026-09-19). R42 IS WITHDRAWN: the bundle was never defective, and I called it one.

### R51. 6 of 4,147 is the CORRECT step-1 gradient of a zero-initialised model.

`of3t-reference` root-caused its own hold and the answer reverses it. **OpenFold3
zero-initialises the output projection and gate of almost every residual branch — 2,271 of
4,890 weight tensors are exactly zero at init — and a zero gate passes zero gradient upstream.**
So a step-1 gradient taken from a random init reaches only the zero-initialised projections
themselves: **6 of 4,147, and the other 4,141 are exactly zero for a correct implementation and
a deleted one alike.**

The bundle was right. **My pass-17 entry called it "the third distinct arrival of the same
failure" and attributed it to a defect in the direct-call path. That reading is withdrawn.**

**And the control I praised was measuring a different thing.** I quoted *"through `pl.Trainer`
in fp32, 4,850 of 4,890 state-dict tensors moved over 20 steps"* as proof their path was fine
and ours broken. It proves nothing of the sort: after step 1 the zero-initialised projections
become non-zero, which lets gradient flow upstream on step 2 onward, so **"moved over 20 steps"
and "6 tensors have a gradient at step 1" are both true of the same correct implementation.** I
compared a 1-step measurement against a 20-step control and read the difference as a defect. **A
control has to match the thing it controls for**, and this one differed in the single dimension
that mattered.

The fix is to take the reference gradient **at trained weights**, and `bundle_min.py` now has
`--checkpoint`.

### K52. Report how many gradient tensors are non-zero. Never the global norm.

The row's own summary of what would have caught this in two seconds, and it is the sharpest
instrument lesson of the campaign. On that bundle the global norm read a healthy **4.64**,
presence was **4,147 of 4,147**, and the finite differences were green — **on a gradient
reaching 0.14 % of the model.** A norm is a sum; it is dominated by whatever is non-zero and
says nothing about how much is. `bundle_min.py` now reports the non-zero tensor count and the
zero-at-init weight count in the manifest.

This supersedes the framing in K44: the FD sampling rule was not the root cause, it was a second
reason the same truth stayed hidden. The root cause was **asking a random init for a gradient**.

### R52. Our shipped LR wiring is off by one step, and the rung I called uninformative is what detects it.

`of3t-gradients` at stack scope on the real model, update rule pinned to theirs (Adam, lr
1.8e-3, betas 0.9/0.95, eps 1e-8, no weight decay, clip 10.0, `AlphaFoldLRScheduler` at
`base_lr` 0): **`recipes.py:119` wires `af3_lr(s)` while `AdamW.step` increments before it
reads, so our step 1 runs at `lr(1)` where theirs runs at `lr(0)`.** The shipped phase reads
**2.106 at k=2 against 0.515** for theirs, and **our `d_1` is 0.0139 where theirs is exactly 0**.

This is a real defect in the update rule, and it inverts §7a. I wrote that k=1 is *structurally
non-discriminating* because `d_1 = 0` on both sides — true only of a **correct** implementation.
Under the shipped wiring `d_1 != 0`, and **that is the detection**. The protocol is amended: k=1
is non-discriminating only when both sides read zero, and a non-zero `d_1` is itself the
finding.

### The rest of that run, all confirmations.

**§7 passes at stack scope in all four arms** — two warmups by two schedule phases, growth
exponents **-0.015, -0.488, -0.067, -0.531**, all sub-linear, worst per-tensor 0.743. Divergence
decays in k, so there is no wiring defect beyond R52, and the magnitude is instrument A's
pair-track miss arriving downstream.

**K16 measured a second time, independently:** scaling one tensor's gradient by 1.01 at every
step moves the trajectory 0.448339 -> 0.448966 and **does not fire**, while the zeros control
reads 1.0000 exactly and does. Adam's scale invariance is now a twice-measured property of this
stack, not a one-off.

**And §7a's second arm earned itself.** The shipped-warmup displacement reads **0.810, outside
AdamW's own 0.9-1.1 band, because 20 steps at lr about k x 1.8e-06 move each element less than
bf16 spacing**; the scaled arm reads 0.995 and 1.001. Running the trajectory twice — shipped
configuration and a warmup scaled for dynamic range — is what kept the shipped arm's result
interpretable instead of quietly noise-dominated.

`of3t-gradients`, runtime census on `of3t-reference`'s frozen 5nw3 batch, **sha256-verified
before it is opened**, over all sixteen shipped (stage, dataset) pairs.

**Seven of the eight terms fire with a non-zero weight AND a non-zero gradient seed.** `bond`
fires **nowhere**: 5nw3 carries no inter-token bond, so `finetune_1` and `finetune_2` hand it

steps"* — on ten of the sixteen pairs, and it is reported as NOT COVERED rather than counted.

The loss-weight table is now checked against a **real artifact** rather than the yaml it was
built from: the batch's own `loss_weights` agree with
`of3_loss_weights("initial_training", "weighted-pdb")` to **6.71e-10**, the float32 round-trip.

### R53. "All eleven loss terms are non-zero" was wrong, and I quoted it approvingly four times.

`of3t-reference` chose 5nw3 as *"the smallest corpus entry on which all eleven loss terms are
non-zero"*, and I repeated that as exemplary batch selection — §6 driving the choice of batch,
the right way round. **Their `LossWeights` declares EIGHT fields**, the frozen batch carries
eight, one of them `bond: 0.0`, and **at most seven are non-zero**. The bundle MANIFEST does not
match its own artifact.

The selection is still defensible on seven terms; the claim attached to it was not, and the
number was checkable against the batch the whole time. **A rationale is not evidence, and I
propagated one because it was well-phrased.**

### R54. `mse` drops upstream's entity weighting, and only a gradient census can see it.

`objectives._TERMS['mse']` never passes `is_dna`, `is_rna` or `is_ligand` to `losses.mse`, so
upstream's **5.0 / 5.0 / 10.0** entity weighting is silently dropped. On this batch, which
carries two ligand tokens, **the value moves 0.233 relative and the gradient seed 0.764**.

**The term fires either way.** A coverage check that reads the weight, or even one that checks
the term contributed something, passes this — which is precisely the failure mode §6 was written
against, arriving at the one place the protocol did not name. Recorded as **D12**.

### K53. `> 0` is not a zero test, and the control caught it before the model did.

With the prediction set equal to the ground truth, `mse`'s gradient is **algebraically zero**
and reads **1.5206e-15**. A `seed > 0.0` test therefore reported the term as **still firing**,
and the negative control — not the model — is what exposed it.

The floor is now **1e-12**: nine orders under the smallest live seed on this batch and three
over the numerical dust, and both coordinate-seeded terms are now correctly rejected. **Any
"did it fire" test in floating point needs a floor chosen against the live signal and the dust,
and the control is what tells you where both are.**

### §6's file-level half is clean where it names, and honest about where it does not.

**Zero in-function `import ttnn` remains in any `openfold3*.py`** — both sites §6 names by line
are gone. 27 remain elsewhere in `tt_bio`, 12 of them in `protenix.py`; the four in
`tt_bio/train/` are the host/device transfer helpers and the DP all-reduce, which move raw
handles by design. Naming the survivors and why they are allowed is the difference between a
clean check and a check that was scoped until it passed.

### The bundle hold is now right for the wrong reason, and that has been flagged.

`MANIFEST.json` still reads `GRADIENT ARTIFACT ON HOLD -- only 6 of 4147 parameter tensors
carry a non-zero gradient` — a true number with a **false implication**, now that R51 has shown
6 of 4,147 is the correct step-1 gradient of a zero-initialised model.

**The hold should stay**: that gradient is taken at random init and is uninformative for
instrument A, so nothing should compare against it. Only the stated reason needs replacing —
*taken at random init, where 6 of 4,147 is correct and expected; superseded by a re-issue at
trained weights*. As written, the next reader concludes the artifact is broken, which is exactly
what I concluded.

Worth keeping as a pattern: **a correct hold with a wrong reason is more durable than a wrong
hold**, because the artifact stays quarantined while the explanation propagates as fact. The
campaign's compose warns on the hold and quotes the reason verbatim, so the wrong reason was
being reprinted on every run.

## Pass 24 (2026-09-19). A guard that fired on correct behaviour, and a constant of mine that was loosely worded.

A 20-step OF3 warmup runs at lr about `k x 1.8e-06`, which puts **every step under bf16
spacing**, so the device copy legitimately does not move and the cumulative ratio read **0.810
against a (0.9, 1.1) band**. That is the fp32 master working exactly as designed, and the guard
called it a failure.

**A guard that fires on correct behaviour is worse than no guard**, because the next caller
disables it or works around it, and then it is not there for the case it was built for. This is
the mirror image of everything else this campaign has found: not a check that cannot fail, but
one that fails when it should not.

`displacement()` now also returns **the displacement the device cannot show** — half an ulp of
each weight, `2**-8` for bfloat16 — and `check_displacement` **reports rather than raises** when
the master has moved less than that and the ratio is low. Reported, never silently passed.

**Verified in three regimes, because a guard fix has to be shown still to catch its own case:**
a correct short run under resolution does not raise and is flagged `below_resolution`; **a
master that moved plenty while the device did not STILL RAISES**; a healthy long run reads ratio
1.000. Committed as a descendant of `wk/of3t-gradients`, whose branch holds that file's most
recent work — not onto the orchestrator branch, and not onto `wk/of3t`, which is rebuilt from
`origin/main` on every compose and would have lost it (K40, applied rather than re-learned).

### R56. My §3d justification said "8 mantissa bits". Right constant, wrong words.

`of3t-gradients` corrected the same slip in its own displacement note. **bfloat16 keeps 7
explicit mantissa bits**, so its precision is 8 bits including the implicit leading one: the
**ulp at 1.0 is 2^-7 = 7.8e-03** and the **unit roundoff — half an ulp, the bound on one
relative rounding error — is 2^-8 = 3.9e-03**.

**The bar does not move**, and the reason matters more than the correction: accumulated rounding
is bounded by the **unit roundoff**, not by the ulp, and 3.9e-03 was always the unit roundoff.
So `sqrt(48) x 3.9e-03 = 2.7e-02` stands and the 5.0e-02 per-tensor bar is still one doubling
above the bf16 floor. Had the ulp been the right quantity, `sqrt(48) x 7.8e-03 = 5.4e-02` would
have put the floor **above** my own bar and made it unachievable — the K33 failure again — so
this was worth checking rather than waving through.

Wording fixed in §3d so nobody re-derives from "8 mantissa bits" and lands on 2^-7. The row's
note needed the opposite correction: there the **ulp** was the right quantity and 3.9e-03 was
the wrong number.

### R57. `of3t-gradients` concluded correctly and left instrument A's magnitude half and D8 with no owner.

It was right to conclude: it measured everything reachable without a usable reference, and it
raised eight items rather than papering over them. But a conclusion is not the same as a
handover, and two campaign deliverables were left with nobody on them:

- **instrument A's magnitude half**, which is the measurement the whole campaign exists for and
  which needs only the gradient `of3t-reference` is re-issuing at trained weights;
- **D8**, the pair track failing in composition — the largest open technical blocker, localised
  by that row to triangle attention injecting rather than inheriting the error, with
  `fp32_softmax` accounting for 3.2x and the in-place residual refuted.

**Re-armed using the fleet's own mechanism rather than a reminder to a future orchestrator.**
`DEPENDS_ON` moves from `of3t-leaves` (satisfied) to `of3t-reference`, and the concluded marker
is removed. `task_depends` holds the row while the named slug lacks a marker and **releases it
on the first tick after the marker appears** — so the work re-enters the queue exactly when its
input exists, with no polling and nothing for me to remember.

This is the third time a row has concluded on an honest blocker and left a deliverable behind
(`of3t-equivalence` on the gradient that could not be measured, this row twice). **The pattern
is worth naming: a row concludes on what IT can finish, and the campaign's deliverable is not
the same object.** The orchestrator owns that difference, and `DEPENDS_ON` plus a marker removal
is the cheap way to express it — better than a new row, which would have to rebuild the harness.

Its **item 8** — `check_displacement` raising on a correct short run — is fixed on its own branch
at `7ecfdc5ba` and control-tested in three regimes (R55). Its **bf16 constant** correction is
folded into §3d with the reasoning that the bar does not move, because accumulated rounding is
bounded by the unit roundoff `2^-8` and not by the ulp `2^-7` (R56).

So of the eight items it raised, **eight are now handled** — six in passes 18-23 and two this

## Pass 26 (2026-09-19). The reference gradient is fixed, and it nearly let the campaign pass vacuously.

### R58. Loading trained weights takes the gradient from 6 of 4,147 to 4,140 of 4,147.

`of3t-reference`, root cause confirmed **by the fix rather than by argument**: re-issued with
`of3-p2-155k.pt` loaded, nothing else changed — same batch, same seed, same draws — and the
gradient reaches **4,140 of 4,147** tensors.

**Three further culprits were ruled out by measurement before the fix, not after:** not float64
mode (an fp32 direct call also gives 6), **not the direct call** (their own `OpenFold3AllAtom` +
`pl.Trainer` also gives 6), and not the batch (4hhb at the full 384-token crop also gives 6).
That third-party control retires the last of my pass-17 misattribution cleanly: **their runner
gives 6 at step 1 too.**

The trajectory shows the same mechanism from the other side, and it is a good picture of a
zero-gated network waking up: **0 tensors move at step 1** (lr = 0), **7 at step 2**, **1,702 at
step 3**, **4,267 at step 5**, **4,850 of 4,890 by step 20**. The zero gates open one layer at a
time. It also confirms §9/A9 empirically — k=2 is where discrimination begins, and k=3 is where
it becomes substantial.

### R59 is the near-miss, and it is the largest of the campaign.

In the row's own words: **instrument A must not be performed on a step-1 gradient from a random
init, because 4,141 of 4,147 per-tensor comparisons would be zero against zero and the gate
would pass with our trunk deleted.**

That is the campaign's central claim passing **vacuously**, on the exact failure this protocol
was written against — `parity-gate-builds-both-sides-from-the-same-source`, §3e's "which check
fails if our model is replaced by zeros?", and the reason §3a insists the unmapped set be
enumerated on both sides. Every one of those guards was in place and **none of them would have
caught this**, because the comparison would have been well-formed, fully populated, and
agreeing.

What catches it is **K52's count**: report how many tensors are non-zero, never the norm. On the
old bundle that count was 6 and the norm was a healthy 4.64.

**Still not published**, and correctly so: at trained weights the finite-difference check at
h = 1e-5 gives **median relative error 0.353**, which is truncation on a curved surface rather
than a wrong gradient. An h-sweep from 1e-3 to 1e-7 is running to pick the right h. A reference
is not published until its own validation is sound.

### R60 / D14. The taped trunk exceeds L1 at crop 384 — their SMALLEST training crop — and no shipped flag moves it.

`of3t-perf`, four probe artifacts, one arm each, crop 384 batch 1, qb2 p300c, AICLK 1350 sampled
during. The clash is in `triangle_multiplication_start`'s `minimal_matmul`
(`tenstorrent.py:5890` via 6706) **at program creation**: statically allocated circular buffers
clash with L1 buffers on `[(0,0)-(10,9)]`, L1 buffer at 884736 against a static CB region ending
at 1159680.

| arm | result |
|---|---|
| shipped defaults | clash 884736 / 1159680 |
| `TT_BIO_RESIDUAL_L1=0` | **identical** clash, same addresses, different program id |
| + `TRIMUL_MASK_L1=0`, `TRIMUL_GATED_MOVE_L1=0`, `TRANSITION_L1_ROWS=0` | still 884736 / 1159680, plus two absorbed |

**So it is not one placement flag**, and `RESIDUAL_L1` — this row's prime suspect since pass 2 —
is **demoted on measurement rather than on argument**, which is the habit worth copying.

The mechanism is the one PTX already paid for: **the tape keeps what the forward frees**
(`autograd.py:155` evicts an L1-resident activation instead of releasing it), which inverted
PTX's L1-placement levers under differentiation. In OF3 it is **a hard failure rather than a
slowdown**, and it lands on `TriangleMultiplication` rather than on the Transition.

**384 is their smallest training crop.** 640 and 768 follow. This is now the blocker on training
OF3 at any size their own recipe uses, and it sits alongside `of3t-memory`'s finding that the
taped ladder stops between 384 and 640 with the fp32-softmax row blocks holding 96 % of the
retained set.

## Pass 27 (2026-09-19). D14 had no owner, and it is the one that decides whether the campaign can finish.

### `of3t-l1` dispatched.

The taped trunk exceeding L1 at crop 384 is the campaign's hardest blocker — **384 is the
smallest crop upstream's own recipe trains at**, so until it clears, there is no training run at
any size they use, and both the model-scope gradient comparison and every perf number are
downstream of it. The three rows that characterised it (`of3t-perf`, `of3t-memory`,
`of3t-tape`) have all concluded, so nobody was on it.

The brief is written to stop it re-deriving what is already known, which is most of its value:

- **What is refuted, with the evidence**: not one placement flag (`TT_BIO_RESIDUAL_L1=0` gives
  an *identical* clash at the *same* addresses, and three further flags change nothing — the
  standing prime suspect demoted on measurement), and not the in-place pair residual (aliasing
  `ttnn.add_` leaves every figure bit-identical).
- **What is known about the mechanism**: the tape keeps what the forward frees
  (`autograd.py:155`), which PTX saw *invert* its L1-placement levers — the Transition going
  from 1.19-1.29x faster to 0.83-0.85x slower — and which here is a **hard failure** on
  `TriangleMultiplication` rather than a slowdown on the Transition.
- **What is already measured**: at 384 one block retains 3.566 GB across 329 live DRAM buffers
  against 0.357 GB and 122 shipped, the fp32-softmax row-block count is 96 % of the retained
  set, and per-block checkpointing is not optional at any crop.

Its criterion is a ladder — 384, then 640, then 768 — and its gate **rejects a rung reported in
one unit**, because between 384 and 640 the count curve overtakes the byte curve and a rung
given only in bytes hides which limit bound it. Correctness is fenced in both directions: the
gradient must stay inside §3d against a float64 reference, and inference must stay
**byte-identical** against a detached `origin/main` checkout **on the same card**. UNIFIED,
since `autograd.py` and the trimul path are shared with four other models, with one measurement
each rather than an assumption.

**Eleven rows now.** This is the fourth dispatched from a finding rather than chartered, and the
pattern across all four is the same: a row concluded honestly on what it could finish, and the
campaign's next question was not the same object as that row's deliverable.

## Pass 29 (2026-09-19). Finite differences cannot validate a recycled trunk gradient, and §3c mandated that they must.

### R62. The 0.353 median was neither their bug nor ours: FD and the analytic gradient are different derivatives.

`of3t-reference`'s h-sweep resolves it. Their trunk runs **`num_recycles + 1` = 4 passes over
the same weights and tapes only the last** (`model.py:230`,
`enable_grad = is_grad_enabled and is_final_iter`). So a **finite difference perturbs the weight
in every cycle and measures the TOTAL derivative**, while **the analytic gradient is
deliberately the PARTIAL derivative through the final cycle**. No choice of `h` reconciles two
different functions.

Four signatures, all consistent with that and with nothing else:

- the difference quotient is **flat from h = 1e-3 to 1e-6**, where a truncation error would
  fall;
- it is **larger** than analytic;
- the factor is **entry-specific** — 5.95x on
  `pairformer_stack.blocks.2.tri_mul_in.layer_norm_in.bias`, 1.53x on
  `blocks.41.tri_mul_out.linear_a_g`;
- it is **absent outside the recycling loop**: diffusion-module entries converge properly over
  the same sweep, 1.785e-08 at h = 1e-4 rising to 1.204e-05 at h = 1e-7 as roundoff takes over,
  which is the shape a healthy sweep has.

**Validation runs at `num_recycles = 0`**, where the taped and untaped functions coincide.

### This is the first amendment that corrects an instrument the PROTOCOL MANDATED.

§3c is the campaign's foundation stone: *"a float64 reference that is itself validated against
float64 central finite differences... never against another approximation."* Ten amendments so
far have moved a scope, a bar's wording, a fitting range or a claim. **A11 says the mandated
validation is, for one part of this model, measuring the wrong thing** — and it does not weaken
the requirement, it narrows where the requirement can be met and says what to do instead.

Worth noting what would have happened without the sweep. The row could have reported *"FD
validates the reference at 1.08e-04"* from the diffusion entries alone, since those converge
beautifully, and the trunk entries would have been dismissed as noise. **The tell was
h-independence**, and only a sweep across three decades shows it — a single `h` cannot.

### R63. §4a is sharpened: the recycle count changes what the gradient MEANS.

Until now §4a said the random draws, including the recycle count, are inputs to the update rule
that must be pinned and matched across stacks. That understates it. **A reference taken at 3
recycles and compared against ours at 0 would disagree with no bug anywhere**, because the two
are different derivatives of the same weights — and the disagreement would look exactly like a
trunk defect, entry-specific and large.

So the recycle count is not only an input to match; it is part of the **definition of the
quantity being compared**, and any gradient artifact has to state it as prominently as it states
the seed.

### K55. A neighbouring campaign's push aborted this composition, and the fetch was too wide.

`compose_verify.sh` began with a bare `git fetch -q origin`, which failed outright —
`cannot lock ref refs/remotes/origin/wk/pvx-eligibility` — because another campaign's worker was
updating its own refs at that moment. The compose exited nonzero for a reason with **nothing to
do with OF3T**, and the output gave no hint of that: it looked like a campaign failure.

Narrowed to this campaign's own refs (main, the eleven row branches, the orchestrator branch)
with one retry. **A genuine failure on our own refs is still loud; a neighbour's concurrent push
is no longer our problem.**

Worth generalising on a fleet where a dozen campaigns share one origin: **fetch what you read,
not everything**, or your tooling inherits every other campaign's timing.

## Pass 30 (2026-09-19). Which recorded FD validations does A11 invalidate? Audited: none, and the reason matters.

A11 says finite differences cannot validate a recycled trunk gradient. The campaign has **three
recorded FD validations** predating it, all `of3t-tape`'s, and a cross-cutting question only the
orchestrator was placed to ask: **are they now void?**

Audited rather than assumed:

| artifact | best relative | control rejected at | bar |
|---|---|---|---|
| `gradcheck_triangle_attention_fp32` | **8.710e-03** | 3.391e-01 | 0.2 |
| `gradcheck_template_block` | **1.012e-02** | 3.266e-01 | 0.2 |
| `gradcheck_template_embedder` | **2.002e-02** | 3.467e-01 | 0.2 |

**All three stand.** Each was taken on a **standalone module invocation** — one forward, one
backward — and the recycling loop lives at model scope in
`projects/of3_all_atom/model.py:224-234`, wrapping `self.template_embedder(...)` and the rest
of the trunk inside `for cycle_no in range(num_cycles)`. A module invoked directly is not
invoked `num_cycles` times, so FD and the analytic gradient are the same derivative there and
the validation is sound.

**But the scope qualifier is now load-bearing and was not stated before.** Those numbers
validate *a single non-recycled invocation of the module*. They do **not** validate that
module's gradient **as it appears in the recycled trunk**, because at trunk scope the quantity
itself changes — FD measures the total derivative across all cycles, the tape produces the
partial through the last.

So this is a **second, independent reason module-scope results do not compose into a trunk-scope
claim**, alongside R36's measured one (sub-modules inside the 0.05 bar composing into a block at
4.3e-01 to 1.4e+00). The first is numerical and the second is definitional: even with perfect
arithmetic, the module-scope gradient and the trunk-scope gradient of the same weight are
different quantities under recycling.

**Recorded because the risk is quiet.** Three passing gradchecks at 8.7e-03 to 2.0e-02, with
controls rejected above 3.2e-01, read exactly like evidence that the trunk's gradients are
sound. They are not that, they were never claimed to be, and nothing in the artifacts said so
until now. The evidence table now carries the qualifier.

## Pass 31 (2026-09-19). With the tape gaps closed, a taped OF3 cycle does not fit one p300c at ANY of their crops.

### R64. The activation wall is gone and a capacity wall is behind it. `of3t-perf`, concluded.

Measured on the composition at `249cba371`, which carries `of3t-tape`'s five fixes including the
parameterised `_FUSED_UNARY_PARAM[MUL_UNARY_SFPU]` that row asked for:

| arm | result |
|---|---|
| crop 128 | **L1 clash** in `minimal_matmul`, L1 buffer 1114112 vs CB region end 1159680 |
| crop 256 | **L1 clash**, 262144 vs 307712 |
| crop 384 | **DRAM OOM** in `transition_z`'s swiglu: **25165824 B wanted, 1079616 B free** |
| crop 384, `--cycles 1` | **identical** DRAM OOM, same allocated byte count |
| crop 384, `--clear-caches` | **identical** DRAM OOM, same allocated byte count |

`of3t-tape`'s own backward runs at 76 tokens, so **the L1 wall appears between 76 and 128**, and
**384 — the smallest crop their recipe uses — runs out of DRAM.** This escalates D14 from "an L1
clash at 384" to **"a taped cycle does not fit one p300c at any crop upstream trains at"**.

**Two candidate explanations raised and both killed by measurement rather than argument**, which
is what makes the finding usable:

- **Not the `no_grad` prefix.** `--cycles 1` removes it entirely — a legitimate
  `num_recycles = 0` draw — and the allocated byte count at failure is **identical** to the
  four-cycle arm.
- **Not warmed caches**, and the row built the instrument to say so. The capture fold runs a real
  `predict_one`, so modules arrive holding memoised device tensors; `--clear-caches` freed **216
  tensors from 324 dicts for 31.0 MB**, DRAM 1544.9 -> 1513.9 MB, **against a shortfall of about
  2.7 GB**. A bounded confound, measured and dismissed rather than assumed away.

So the retention is **the taped cycle's own activations**. The row states plainly that this is
`of3t-memory`'s ladder and `of3t-tape`'s retention policy jointly, is not reachable from its own
namespace, and **proposes no lever** — correct scope discipline, and both those rows have
concluded, so it lands on `of3t-l1`.

### R65. The h-sweep evidence, and the explanation predicts its own null case.

`of3t-reference`'s `hsweep.json`, six entries at trained weights, h from 1e-3 to 1e-7, float64:

| entry | fd/analytic | spread over h |
|---|---|---|
| `pairformer_stack.blocks.2.tri_mul_in.layer_norm_in.bias` | **5.976** | 2.0e-02 |
| `pairformer_stack.blocks.1.pair_transition.layer_norm.weight` | **5.844** | 8.4e-02 |
| `msa_module.blocks.0.msa_att_row.linear_v.weight` | **1.697** | **0** |
| `pairformer_stack.blocks.41.tri_mul_out.linear_a_g.weight` | **1.531** | 5.5e-06 |
| `pairformer_stack.blocks.41.tri_att_start.layer_norm.weight` | **1.013** | — |
| `diffusion_module...blocks.8.attention_pair_bias.mha.linear_o` | best rel **1.785e-08** | converges |

**The entry at 1.013 is the explanation's own positive control**, and it is the detail that
makes A11 more than a plausible story. If FD measures the total derivative across all cycles
while the tape gives the partial through the last, then a parameter whose **earlier-cycle
contribution is negligible** must show a ratio of about 1 — and one does. The theory predicts
where there should be **no** anomaly, and there is none there.

A spread of exactly **0** across three decades of h on the MSA entry is the other half: that is
not truncation behaving badly, it is a different function being measured exactly.

## Pass 32 (2026-09-19). The peak is in the MSA module, not the trunk, and only one of three block stacks was checkpointed.

### R66. `of3t-l1`'s first measurement moves the target everyone had been aiming at.

At crop 384 the taped OF3 cycle **exhausts all 34.217 GB of a p300c across 4977 live DRAM
allocations**, and — the part that matters — **the peak is set inside the MSA module, before the
template stack or the 48-block trunk has run** (`perf/of3t_l1/out/base_384.json`, qb2 p300c,
AICLK median 1350 sampled during).

The whole campaign, this row's brief and my own summaries have all said *"the taped trunk"*. The
trunk is not where it breaks. **Only one of the three block stacks had been offered to
`ops.checkpoint_segment`** at all; the other two now are.

**What made it findable is an instrument detail worth copying:** `perf/of3t_l1/ladder.py`
reports the live allocation **count** and the byte high-water **together**, keeps **DRAM and L1
apart**, and **tags the peak with the block stack that was running when it was set**. A
high-water number without that tag says a model is too big; with it, it says which third of the
model to look at.

### K56. A checkpointed segment must not overwrite its own input, because the recompute reads input VALUES.

The MSA block was writing its own input (`own_m`). That is now gone and the m residual always
lands in the update buffer — **bit-identical**, since bf16 addition is commutative and the code
comment already said so, and at **the same peak**. It is not an optimisation; it is a
precondition.

The reason generalises beyond this block: **`checkpoint_segment` recomputes the forward in the
backward from the saved inputs, so a segment that mutated its input differentiates the wrong
function.** Any in-place write to a segment boundary is therefore a correctness bug the moment
checkpointing is switched on, and it is silent until then — the forward is fine, the memory is
fine, and only the gradient is wrong.

And the inference path is untouched by construction: with no hook installed,
`checkpoint_segment` is `fn(*inputs)`.

### D14's framing is corrected.

Not "the taped trunk exceeds L1 at 384" and not "the taped trunk does not fit" — **a taped OF3
cycle does not fit, and at 384 the binding peak is in the MSA module.** The L1 clashes at 128
and 256 are separate and remain. Recorded so the next reader does not spend a pass instrumenting
the pairformer stack.

### R67. The bundle flipped to PUBLISHED while its payload was still in transfer, and my audit went green.

`MANIFEST.json` now reads **`status: PUBLISHED. The validated gradient is
grads_f64_recycles0.pt: trained weights, num_recycles pinned to 0, 4138 of 4147 tensors
non-zero, agreeing with float64 central differences`** — which is exactly the artifact the
campaign has been waiting for, produced exactly as A11 and K52 prescribe.

**And that file is not on the host.** The manifest's own per-file flags say
`grads_f64_recycles0.pt: on_qb2 = "in transfer"`, along with four others, and the only large
file on qb2 is `grads_f64_recycles3.pt.part`. A consumer reading the status line goes to a path
holding a partial download of a **different** artifact.

**My audit reported 0 warnings on it**, because the hold-check looks for the string `HOLD` and
the status no longer contains one. That is the R43 shape — headline and per-file state
disagreeing — **one pass after R43 was fixed, in the same file, and my check was written to
catch R43 specifically rather than the class.**

Fixed: whenever the status claims publication the audit now reads the declared `on_qb2` flags
and warns on any artifact that is not present. It reports the four immediately.

**`of3t-gradients` stays held**, and it is held for the right reason after all — not because
`of3t-reference` has not concluded, but because the artifact it consumes is not yet fetchable. I
had been about to release it on the strength of the status line and checked the host first. **A
status field is a claim about the world; the host is the world.**

unrelated work.

### Why every property of that artifact matters, recorded in the brief so the row does not have to rediscover it.

- **Trained weights.** At a random init OF3 zero-initialises the output projection and gate of
  nearly every residual branch, so a step-1 gradient reaches **6 of 4,147 tensors — correctly**.
  A comparison there would have been 4,141 zeros against 4,141 zeros and **would have passed
  with our trunk deleted** (R59).
- **`num_recycles` pinned to 0.** Their trunk runs `num_recycles + 1` passes and tapes only the
  last, so finite differences measure the **total** derivative while the analytic gradient is
  the **partial** through the final cycle (A11). A comparison at mismatched recycle counts
  disagrees with no bug anywhere and looks exactly like a trunk defect.
- **4138 of 4147 non-zero, reported as a count.** The earlier bundle had a healthy-looking
  global norm of 4.64 on a gradient reaching **0.14 %** of the model (K52).

### K57. Watch a transfer finish; do not read that it finished.

The manifest said `PUBLISHED` while the file was a `.part`, and it said so for at least two
passes. What settled it was `stat` on the host twice, 45 seconds apart, and then polling to
completion — total cost about eight minutes of one turn, against a campaign-central artifact
that had been notionally "published" and unusable.

Two samples also distinguish **slow** from **stalled**, which one sample cannot, and a stalled
transfer is indistinguishable from a slow one right up until it never finishes.

### R68. The reference is VALIDATED, and ten of the twelve check entries are inside the trunk.

`of3t-reference`, `b1c03cb16`. `grads_f64_recycles0.pt` validated against float64 central finite
differences at **h = 1e-4, 12 entries, max relative error 2.18e-03, median 4.17e-04** — **23x
inside the 5.0e-02 bar** — and **ten of the twelve entries are inside the pairformer trunk**,
worst at `pairformer_stack.blocks.46.pair_stack.tri_mul_in.layer_norm_out.weight`.

That last detail is what closes A11 properly. The concern was that FD could not validate a
recycled trunk gradient; pinning `num_recycles = 0` does not merely dodge the problem, it makes
**the trunk itself** checkable, and the validation is now concentrated where the campaign's
doubt was rather than on the heads that always converged.

Artifact: trained `of3-p2-155k`, batch 5nw3 at 56 tokens, loss **1.6591175475821072** and
**bit-identical on replay**, **4,138 of 4,147 non-zero, 0 absent**, global norm
**3.908301894520238**, `clip_coef` 1.0.

**`grads_f64_recycles3.pt` is published deliberately separately** — the gradient at the recycle
count their config actually draws — **and labelled as not finite-difference validatable**,
rather than quietly mixed in with the validated one. That is A11 applied to publication rather
than just to measurement, and it is the right shape: a shipped-config comparison needs it and
must know what it cannot lean on.

### R69. Three keys the checkpoint does not supply, and w_0 equality depends on them.

`version_tensor` and two `diffusion_transformer.layer_norm_z.weight` tensors **stay at their
random init** because the checkpoint has no entry for them. They are named in the manifest, and
**our side must end up with the same two unset or the two stacks do not start from the same
`w_0`** — which would make every downstream comparison a comparison of different runs.

A quiet precondition of the whole campaign's central claim, found only because someone
enumerated what the checkpoint did **not** contain. The natural check is over what is loaded;
this one is over what is missing.

### Transfer and cost discipline, both worth the record.

Both files were **hash-verified end to end** — computed on the rented box, computed again on
qb2, identical — and **qb2 now pulls straight from the box, so pc at 97 % full is out of the
path**. The A100 is **destroyed, zero instances running**, 3.1 h of rental, credit **36.44 ->
32.92** across the entire row. A campaign that rents hardware and leaves nothing running is
worth noting precisely because the failure is silent and expensive.

## Pass 35 (2026-09-19). The L1 clash at 384 is cleared, the cost is named, and the wall moves to a shard-count limit.

### R70. `evict-on-read` clears the circular-buffer clash, and the row prices it rather than declaring victory.

`of3t-l1`, qb2 card 0 p300c, AICLK median 1350 sampled during. **Backward L1 holders drop to
three**, all of them the non-evictable set and **none at a clash address**, so the
circular-buffer clash that blocked crop 384 is **gone**.

**The cost is stated in the same breath**: DRAM rises to **21.003 GB / 4974 live allocations**
from **15.623 GB / 4653** — the evicted copies. That is the change's own price, quoted by the
row that made the change rather than discovered later by someone else. It is also still under
the 34.217 GB card, so DRAM is no longer the binding constraint at this rung.

**The wall moved rather than fell.** The backward now fails elsewhere: `ttnn.sum` inside a
broadcast-add backward raising **`num_shards <= num_cores`, 512 shards along height against 64
cores**. That is a sharding constraint, not a capacity one — a different and more tractable
shape of failure than "does not fit".

So D14's L1 half is cleared at 384 and the crop-384 blocker is now a shard-count limit in one
op's backward. The L1 clashes at 128 and 256 have not been re-measured against this lever and
should be.

**Worth noting what this does to the campaign's bound.** Since pass 31 the honest statement has
been *"a taped OF3 cycle does not fit one p300c at any crop their recipe uses"*. That is still
true as of this measurement — 384 fails — but the **reason** has changed, and a shard-count
error on one op is a much smaller claim than a capacity ceiling. The bound stands; its
foundation is narrower.
